entries.appliesTo: Alabama public K-12 schools (elementary, middle, high) and the State Department of Education

sources.curriculum: § 16-46B-2(a)(1)-(3) — 'each public high school shall offer at least one authentic computer science course from a department-approved list' … 'each public middle school shall offer instruction in middle school computer science courses approved by the department' … 'each public elementary school shall offer instruction on the basics of computer science and computational thinking.'
sources.graduationReq: § 16-46B-7(c)(1) — 'Beginning with the graduating class of 2032, all public school students shall demonstrate digital literacy by earning at least one credit in a department-approved, high school or college-level computer science course, or by completing a department-approved course with embedded computer science skills and experiences.'
sources.enforcer: § 16-46B-2(e) — 'The enforcement of this section shall comply with Section 16-1-11.1.'

flags: AI content is limited to the amended definition of computer science: § 16-46B-1(2) — 'their emerging technologies, including, but not limited to, artificial intelligence'; the bill is otherwise a general computer science graduation-requirement act

State Department of Education carries administrative duties (§ 16-46B-7(c)(1) — 'The department shall develop and publish a set of minimum standards…' and 'shall publish a list of… courses… that have been approved'), which bind an agency rather than schools; retained under education category since the regime targets K-12 curricula
graduation requirement adds no credits: § 16-46B-7(c)(1) — 'This requirement shall not result in an increase in the number of credits required for graduation.'
no penalty stated; enforcement routed by cross-reference only (rule 4 — no penaltyMax coded)
Effective October 1, 2026 (Section 2 — 'This act shall become effective on October 1, 2026.'); graduation requirement begins with the class of 2032
